categories.main_business_segments: Welltower operates through three primary business segments: Seniors Housing Operating, Triple-net, and Outpatient Medical. The Seniors Housing Operating segment includes various types of senior living communities managed by third-party operators. The Triple-net segment consists of properties leased to operators under long-term, triple-net leases, including seniors housing and post-acute care facilities. The Outpatient Medical segment comprises multi-tenant medical office buildings and outpatient facilities, primarily leased to healthcare providers.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Welltower's core business is real estate investment, development, and management, with a focus on healthcare infrastructure. The company utilizes an UPREIT structure and invests through acquisitions, developments, and joint ventures. It leverages master lease structures, RIDEA arrangements for operating properties, and asset management processes that include financial monitoring, property inspections, and compliance reviews. Sustainability and energy efficiency technologies are increasingly integrated into property operations.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Welltower primarily serves seniors housing operators, post-acute care providers, health systems, and healthcare service providers. Its end markets include senior living residents, patients in post-acute and long-term care, and healthcare professionals and systems utilizing outpatient medical facilities. Major customers include large operators such as Sunrise Senior Living, Cogir Management Company, Oakmont Management Group, and Integra Healthcare Properties.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates in major, high-growth markets across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Its portfolio is diversified geographically, with significant concentrations in California, Florida, Texas, the U.K., and Canada. As of December 31, 2024, Welltower owned or had interests in over 2,100 properties across these regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: Welltower operates as an owner, developer, and lessor of healthcare real estate, positioning itself downstream in the healthcare supply chain. It provides the physical infrastructure that enables healthcare delivery but does not directly provide healthcare services. The company partners with operators and health systems who deliver care to end users.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Welltower's strategic focus is on transforming healthcare infrastructure to support innovative care delivery models and improve wellness outcomes. The company emphasizes portfolio diversification, sustainability, and ESG leadership, as well as investments in high-growth markets and property types. R&D initiatives include sustainability projects, energy efficiency upgrades, and the integration of technology and data analytics to enhance asset management and operational performance.
categories.revenue_model: Welltower generates revenue primarily through resident fees and services (from operating properties), rental income from long-term leases (triple-net and outpatient medical), interest income from real estate loans, and, to a lesser extent, gains on property sales. The company also earns management fees and participates in joint venture earnings. Its REIT structure requires the distribution of a significant portion of taxable income as dividends.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Welltower competes with other healthcare REITs, private equity and hedge funds, real estate partnerships, insurance companies, banks, and healthcare operators for property acquisitions and tenants. Major competitors include Ventas, Healthpeak Properties, and other large healthcare-focused REITs. Welltower is positioned as a market leader with a large, diversified portfolio and strong relationships with top operators.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2024, Welltower had total assets of $51.0 billion and reported net income attributable to common stockholders of $952 million for the year. Funds from operations (FFO) were $2.3 billion, and consolidated net operating income (NOI) was $3.2 billion. The company demonstrated strong growth, with net income and FFO increasing significantly year-over-year, driven by acquisitions, development activity, and improved operating performance.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Welltower differentiates itself through its scale, diversified portfolio, and partnerships with leading healthcare operators and systems. The company emphasizes its ability to provide high-quality, sustainable healthcare real estate in attractive markets, supporting innovative care models and wellness outcomes. Its focus on ESG leadership, operational excellence, and strategic capital allocation enhances its value proposition to investors, operators, and healthcare providers.
